overall: The AG found three violations: October 26, 2021 minutes lacked the meeting time and document list, a July 2021 email exchange amounted to deliberation between a quorum, and one complaint was not distributed within 14 business days; other allegations were dismissed or declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleging no roll call votes and inaccurate minutes at two November 2021 meetings, filed January 2022, was challenged as untimely.
allegations.key_passage: Since these allegations could have been discovered more than 30 days before the complaint was filed, we decline to review this complaint.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the notice for a June 22, 2021 meeting listed no topics and was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: When a public body does not actually meet, the public body cannot violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to an insufficiently specific notice, even if the notice would have been insufficiently specific had the public body proceeded with its deliberation.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the notice for a December 14, 2021 meeting should have identified which meeting minutes would be approved.
allegations.key_passage: As the Committee did not meet on that date, we find no violation.

allegations.summary: Alleged the October 26, 2021 minutes were inaccurate; the AG found they were substantially accurate and detailed enough.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee substantially complied with the requirement that it provide an accurate and sufficiently detailed summary of the discussion that occurred during the October 26, 2021, meeting.

allegations.summary: The October 26, 2021 minutes omitted the meeting time and a list of documents used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: However, we find that the Committee failed to include the time of the meeting and a list of documents used during the meeting

allegations.summary: Alleged that a June 4, 2021 email from the chair to two other members about a topic for a future meeting was deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that this email does not constitute deliberation, as it fits within the exception to the definition of deliberation for the distribution of meeting agenda information.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the chair's emails to the full committee responding to complaints were deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that this email was necessitated by the Open Meeting Law, and find no violation.

allegations.summary: Alleged deliberation outside a posted meeting through a July 15, 2021 email chain in which a member stated how she would vote before a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: one member’s statement to another in advance of a meeting as to how she planned to vote at the meeting constituted a communication between a quorum of the Committee on public business within the Committee’s jurisdiction, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Alleged the chair failed to distribute an October 6, 2021 complaint to the third member within 14 business days.
Alleged the chair failed to distribute an October 29, 2021 complaint to all members within 14 business days.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Chair did distribute the October 29, 2021, complaint within the required timeframe.

allegations.summary: Alleged the chair should not have responded individually to three complaints from a member.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Chair’s efforts to respond individually to Member Sylbert, where she was authorized to do so, satisfied the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 30 days, amend the October 26, 2021 minutes to include the meeting time and a list of all documents used.
Within 30 days, publicly release the July 15 email chain described in the determination, by reading it at a meeting and listing it in the minutes, or by posting it with the minutes online.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
